steps: Write T = 104, the area of ABC. Because AE:AC = 1:4, area ABE = T/4.
BD:DC = 3:1 gives area ABD = 3T/4 and area ADC = T/4.
Within ADC, E divides AC with AE:AC = 1:4. Hence area ADE = T/16.
ABD and ADE share AD, so their heights are in the ratio 12:1. Since BE crosses AD at P, BP:PE has that same ratio.
ABP therefore takes 12/13 of ABE: area ABP = 3T/13 = 24 cm².
Repeat the argument with the vertex names cycled A→B→C. The three side-division ratios are the same, so BCQ and CAR each also have area 24 cm². The outer triangle need not be equilateral.
ABP, BCQ and CAR have disjoint interiors and fill everything outside PQR. Subtract all three from ABC.
